problem: Map-based training-free navigation with VLM-built semantic maps (VLMaps, OpenMask3D) assumes the map is accurate; when the first retrieval fails, the agent just tries the next highest-confidence location, which shares the same bias and often fails again.
motivation: Visual perception in real environments is noisy and biased, and there are no labels to evaluate map quality. If the top-confidence retrieval fails, other high-confidence regions likely share the same bias, so replanning needs a signal beyond confidence, ideally one that requires no extra labels.
key_idea: After an initial failure, shortlist top-k high-confidence candidates and pick among them using uncertainty (max entropy) or multi-view consistency (min feature standard error / min pairwise KL) instead of the next-highest confidence.
insight: Replanning by confidence alone perpetuates map bias: 'Random from top-2 confidence' beats 'Max confidence (top2)' on OM3D (17.12 vs 17.05). Choosing high-entropy or multi-view-consistent candidates from the shortlist does better, and the ablations show the reverse directions (min entropy, max KL) underperform the baselines. On VLMaps, min stderr gives 77.7-82.7 against 67.0 for max confidence. Shortlisting by top-k category is more robust to k than by confidence.
method: Replan trigger: when the first retrieval or navigation fails, choose a new unvisited location from the fixed map; the first attempt is always max confidence.
Candidate shortlist (top-k): either top-k by confidence for the query class, or top-k category, keeping points whose top-k predicted classes include the target class.
Entropy measure: computes the entropy of each candidate's class distribution and picks the max-entropy candidate, to counter confident-but-biased predictions.

Multi-view consistency: picks the candidate with the lowest channel-averaged feature standard error (SE=1/d Σ σ_k/√m; single-view candidates get infinity) or the lowest mean symmetric pairwise KL across per-view class distributions.
OpenMask3D adaptation: stores all per-view CLIP crop features (up to 5 views, ranked by object pixel count) rather than averaging them, and omits multi-scale crop augmentation.
VLMaps adaptation: precomputes per-cell entropy, stderr and KL using distance-weighted statistics (weighted std, effective sample size); navigation uses the Habitat planner and follower.
Cost: entropy and stderr are O(n), pwKL is O(n²); retrieval takes under 15 ms.

setting.backbone: OpenMask3D (Mask3D + CLIP ViT-L/14, frozen) and VLMaps (LSeg, frozen)
setting.observation: posed RGB(-D) images from pre-exploration, building a 3D point cloud or top-down semantic map
setting.action_space: OM3D: object retrieval only, with path planning and following assumed successful. VLMaps: low-level actions from the Habitat planner and follower to waypoints
setting.privileged: Pre-explored map with known poses; GT used only for evaluation. Oracle baseline uses GT masks (baseline only).

results: On OM3D two-shot retrieval, CARe variants reach up to 18.75% against 17.05% for max confidence (top-2) and 17.12% for the best baseline, with 20 of 25 entries beating the best baseline. On VLMaps, min stderr gets 82.7% subgoal success versus 67.0% for max confidence and 54.4% with no replan.
limitations: Assumes the frozen model has consistent decision biases; updating the model may reduce the gains.
The map is fixed and not updated during replanning.
pwKL is O(n²) and ran out of memory on larger scenes; evaluation is limited to simulation, a single replan step and custom benchmarks without real-robot tests.
